content: For the investigation of suspected Type 6 diabetes in newly diagnosed adults, the following steps should be taken: 1. If there are no clinical features suggestive of monogenic diabetes, proceed to evaluate for characteristics indicative of Type 2 diabetes and perform a C-peptide test. 2. Interpret the C-peptide test results as follows: If the C-peptide level is greater than or equal to 200 pmol/L, this finding suggests the possibility of Type 1 diabetes. In cases where monogenic diabetes remains a clinical suspicion, additional genetic testing should be considered. If the C-peptide level is less than 200 pmol/L, this result confirms the diagnosis of Type 1 diabetes.
